audit.whatIsWrong: Level 1 and Level 6 were given to Graves and 2+ items to Darius, contradicting both the mirrored Darius audit (Darius on six rows, Graves at 2+ items) and the page's own whys — whys[0] opens with 'Darius all-ins level 1' and whys[6] says Graves out-skirmishes him late.
audit.why: The two directions must agree, and here the mirror, the packet chart and the prose all say the same thing while only the side tokens disagreed.
audit.corrected: Levels 1 through first item all Darius (3/10 or 4/10); 2+ items Graves (7/10).

audit.whatIsWrong: The entire page is built on 'punish his Apprehend cooldown' and never once states it.
audit.why: Apprehend is 26/23.5/21/18.5/16s — at rank 1 that is a 26-second window, by far the longest cooldown in his early kit and the reason the in-and-out pattern works at all. Decimate is 9s, Crippling Strike 5s, Noxian Guillotine 120s at rank 1.
audit.corrected: Apprehend is 26s at rank 1 — bait it, then you have most of half a minute to trade. Noxian Guillotine is 120s at rank 1, but it refreshes on a kill, so the number only holds if he misses.
sources: _kits/darius.json E cd 26/23.5/21/18.5/16, Q cd 9/8/7/6/5, R cd 120/100/80 and refresh text

audit.whatIsWrong: Graves' E is called 'Bushwhack' in seven places, and Smoke Screen is called a blind in five. Apprehend's passive armor penetration is never mentioned.
audit.why: Graves' E is Quickdraw, and its True Grit stacks armor and MR while refreshing off his autos. Smoke Screen reduces sight range and briefly slows — Graves has no blind anywhere in his kit. Apprehend passively makes Darius' physical damage ignore a percentage of armor, which directly eats the True Grit stacking the page tells you to rely on.
audit.corrected: Quickdraw's True Grit is your armor, but Apprehend passively pierces a share of it — so stacking resists is a partial answer, not the answer. Smoke Screen slows and cuts his sight on a 26s cooldown at rank 1: keep firing while he is in it rather than expecting his attacks to miss.

audit.why: The in-and-out trade rule and the 'never fight near a wall' rule are both right and both follow from the pull.

edits.before: Darius owns the first three levels outright. His E, Apprehend, pulls you straight into axe-handle range before your second Quickdraw charge exists, and every second you stand in melee he stacks Hemorrhage and lands the empowered outer ring of Decimate to heal off you. Don't last-hit near a wall or a stacked wave he can yank you onto, and respect that his level 1-2 all-in beats your one-ability kit. Your only early job is to farm with the tip of End of the Line from max range and survive to 3, where your second Quickdraw charge and Bushwhack armor finally let you trade back. Until then eat a little poke and never burn Quickdraw chasing a kill you can't finish — you need both charges to disengage.
edits.after: Darius owns the first three levels outright. Apprehend (26s at rank 1) pulls you straight into axe-handle range, and every second you stand in melee he stacks Hemorrhage and lands the empowered outer ring of Decimate to heal off you. Don't last-hit near a wall or a stacked wave he can yank you onto, and respect that his level 1-2 all-in beats your one-ability kit. Your early job is to farm with the tip of End of the Line and survive to 3, where Quickdraw and True Grit armor finally let you trade back — though Apprehend's passive pierces part of that armor, so it blunts him rather than blanking him. Never burn Quickdraw chasing a kill you can't finish; it is your only exit.

edits.before: This is still his window. Darius wins nearly every committed melee all-in from 4 through 9, and at 6 his R, Noxian Guillotine, does true damage that climbs with each Hemorrhage stack and refreshes on a kill — so letting five stacks sit on you turns a clean kite into a flat execute. Use Smoke Screen to blind his empowered Decimate and gut his vision when he steps up, and only trade with Quickdraw in-and-out: dash in for the point-blank magazine, then dash back out before Apprehend comes off cooldown. Never fight near a wall, and never reload inside his pull range. Bait the Q whiff, punish the cooldown, but accept you're playing for farm and a scaling lead, not a level-6 solo kill — your own R is a poke/escape nuke, not a reliable answer to his execute.
edits.after: This is still his window. Darius wins nearly every committed melee all-in from 4 through 9, and at 6 Noxian Guillotine (120s at rank 1) does true damage that climbs with each Hemorrhage stack and refreshes on a kill — so five stacks sitting on you turns a clean kite into a flat execute. Smoke Screen slows him and guts his sight when he steps up; it does not stop his damage, so use it to leave. Trade only in-and-out: dash in for the point-blank magazine, then get out inside Apprehend's 26 seconds. Never fight near a wall, never reload inside pull range. Bait the Q whiff, punish the cooldown, and accept you're playing for farm and a scaling lead, not a level-6 solo kill.

edits.before: Once you hit Eclipse or Youmuu's and stack a second item, the lane flips. Your stacked Bushwhack armor and refreshing Quickdraw charges let you out-skirmish a Darius who has no answer to sustained kiting in the open — his power was always front-loaded into the early all-in, and that window has closed. Fight off the wave and away from walls so Apprehend whiffs, weave double Quickdraw around his Decimate windup, and blind the empowered hit with Smoke Screen on cooldown. You out-DPS and out-sustain him in a drawn-out fight now, and Collateral Damage plus your mobility make you the better skirmisher and roamer — drag the game past laning and you carry the 1v1 he used to win.
edits.after: Once you hit Eclipse or Youmuu's and stack a second item, the lane flips. Stacked True Grit armor and a Quickdraw that refreshes off every landed auto let you out-skirmish a Darius with no answer to sustained kiting in the open — his power was always front-loaded, and that window has closed. Fight off the wave and away from walls so Apprehend whiffs, weave around his Decimate windup, and drop Smoke Screen (26s at rank 1) on the empowered swing so the slow pulls you clear. You out-DPS and out-sustain him in a drawn-out fight now, and Collateral Damage plus your mobility make you the better skirmisher — drag the game past laning and you carry the 1v1 he used to win.
